name: Alpha Strike
strategy: Overwhelm the enemy during the opening Rounds through rapid mobilization, accurate attacks, concentrated volleys, and decisive Charges. Its offensive bonuses decline as the battle develops.

commands.name: First Strike Orders
commands.effect: If the active Unit is within Short of friendly Headquarters, its next Attack this Round gains Accurate X, where X depends on the current Round.

commands.name: Opening Volley
commands.effect: The active Unit gains +X Attacks on its next ranged Attack this Phase, where X is determined by the current Round.

commands.name: Shock Assault
commands.effect: When the active Unit declares a Charge, increase its Charge Impact by X for that Charge, where X depends on the current Round. This does not increase Charge distance.

commands.name: Rapid Mobilization
commands.effect: Choose either Rapid Deployment (Movement, once per battle, Round 1 only) or Standard Orders (Assault/Combat). See rapidMobilizationModes.

commands.name: Ferocious Opening
commands.effect: Choose the active Unit making a Melee Attack this Phase. Gain Critical 2 in Round 1, Critical 1 in Rounds 2–3, or Accurate 1 in Rounds 4–5. CP-granted Critical requires no Surge and does not modify Charge Impact.

doctrineIdentity: Alpha Strike rewards seizing the initiative early in the battle. Its Round 1 offense is strongest, its benefits fall progressively through Round 3, and it retains smaller offensive benefits in Rounds 4–5. Rapid Mobilization offers a once-per-battle way to add one mobile reinforcement during the first Round without changing ordinary Reserves for the rest of the army. It differs from Firing Line through its decreasing ranged bonuses, from Breakthrough through its immediate offensive emphasis rather than sustained Charge reliability, and from Deep Strike because it adds a single early reinforcement instead of placing Units in unexpected locations.

decliningOffensiveBonuses.rule: Unless noted otherwise, the following Alpha Strike bonuses depend on the current Round. The Round determines the bonus each time the Command is used; the bonus does not depend on whether the attacking Unit has previously attacked or fought its target.

rapidDeployment.effect: When you would activate a friendly Unit during the Round 1 Movement Phase, you may instead select one Unit in Reserve. Deploy it wholly within your deployment zone, then perform its normal Movement activation. This arrival is in addition to your normal Round 1 reinforcement allowance, and it ignores the ordinary restrictions preventing Reserve Units from performing Movement actions or declaring Charges on the Round they arrive. The Unit may declare a legal Charge during the ensuing Assault Phase. It does not receive an additional activation. Rapid Deployment may be used only once per battle, even if this Command card later becomes available again.

standardOrders.effect: Choose one friendly Unit. It gains +1 Attack on its next eligible Attack this Phase.

rapidMobilizationModes.commonRules: Both modes use the normal Command CP and card-exhaustion cost. Each use resolves only one of the two modes. Once Rapid Deployment has been used, Standard Orders remains available on later uses of the Command.

commandClarifications.clarification: Provides reliable Hits, but the recipient must be within Short of a friendly Headquarters when the Command is used. Its bonus can apply to an otherwise eligible Attack later in the same Round.
Adds Attack dice to a single ranged Attack by the Unit, not to every Model.
Modifies only the Charge Impact of one declared Charge. It does not increase the Charge distance or the Unit’s later Melee Attack dice.
CP-powered Critical on one Melee Attack in Rounds 1–3; Accurate 1 in Rounds 4–5. Never affects Charge Impact.
None of the four offensive Commands requires that the Unit or its target be attacked for the first time. Only the Round-dependent bonuses decline.
